title: Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)
description:
**About Revun**
 Revun is building a next\-generation software platform designed to modernize how property owners, property managers, brokerages, maintenance providers, service professionals, and real estate organizations operate.
   

  

 The platform combines CRM, leasing, maintenance, accounting, payments, communications, workflow automation, compliance, reporting, AI, integrations, and stakeholder portals into a single operating platform.
   

  

 Our goal is not to build another collection of disconnected software tools. We are building an operational platform that simplifies complex business processes, reduces manual work, improves visibility, and helps organizations operate more efficiently.
   

  

 The product is already underway, and we are now looking for a strong product designer who can help turn a complex platform into an intuitive, professional, scalable, and commercially ready user experience.
   

  

**About The Role**
 Revun is hiring a
 **Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)** 
 to lead the design of our web and mobile product experience.
   

  

 This is not a graphic design role, and it is not a role focused only on creating attractive screens.
   

  

 We are looking for someone who understands how to design real software products, including complex SaaS platforms, marketplace applications, dashboards, workflows, portals, mobile apps, and multi\-user systems.
   

  

 You will work closely with leadership, engineering, and product stakeholders to simplify complex workflows, improve usability, create scalable design systems, and help prepare the platform for commercial launch.
   

  

 The successful candidate must be able to think through product flows, user journeys, permissions, edge cases, responsive layouts, information hierarchy, and design handoff — not just visual styling.
   

  

 You should also be comfortable using AI tools to improve your design process, speed up research and ideation, organize complex requirements, generate UX copy, explore layout options, create user flows, and improve documentation while still applying your own product judgment.
   

  

 How to Apply
   

  

 Please submit your
 **resume and portfolio** 
 for consideration.
   

  

 Your portfolio should include examples of real product\-design work, such as user flows, dashboards, complex interfaces, mobile screens, design systems, marketplace workflows, SaaS platforms, or similar product examples.
   

  

 Candidates with only branding, landing pages, social media graphics, or marketing websites will not be the strongest fit for this role.
   

  

 Qualified candidates will be invited to complete a pre\-recorded video interview 24\-48 hours after applying as the next step in the hiring process.
   

  

 Key Responsibilities
   

  

* Design user\-friendly web and mobile experiences for a complex SaaS and marketplace\-style platform
* Create wireframes, user flows, prototypes, high\-fidelity designs, and developer\-ready UI specifications
* Design workflows for multiple user types, including internal users, property owners, tenants, vendors, service providers, partners, and administrators
* Translate complex business processes into simple, intuitive product experiences
* Work closely with leadership and engineering to turn product vision into clear, usable, buildable designs
* Improve the overall information architecture, navigation, dashboard structure, forms, portals, workflows, and mobile experience
* Design and maintain scalable design systems, reusable components, UI patterns, and style standards
* Create clean, professional, modern, and consistent product interfaces
* Identify gaps, edge cases, confusing user flows, and areas where the product experience can be simplified
* Collaborate with developers to ensure designs are technically feasible and implemented accurately
* Review builds and provide design QA feedback before release
* Use AI tools responsibly to speed up research, ideation, UX writing, documentation, design exploration, and workflow development
* Validate AI\-assisted design outputs through human judgment, user needs, business requirements, and product logic
* Support commercial launch readiness by ensuring the platform is easy to understand, easy to use, and visually consistent


**Required Experience**
* 6\+ years of UX/UI, Product Design, or related digital product design experience
* Experience designing complex SaaS platforms, marketplace applications, CRM systems, workflow platforms, fintech products, operational dashboards, or other multi\-role software products
* Strong experience designing both web and mobile product experiences
* Strong Figma skills, including components, Auto Layout, variants, design systems, prototyping, and developer handoff
* Experience designing dashboards, forms, tables, workflows, portals, user profiles, settings, notifications, and role\-based user experiences
* Experience working directly with engineers and product stakeholders
* Strong understanding of user flows, information architecture, interaction design, usability, visual hierarchy, responsive design, and design systems
* Experience using AI tools to support design work, UX writing, research synthesis, user\-flow creation, wireframing, prototyping, or product documentation
* Ability to explain design decisions clearly and connect them to user needs, business goals, and technical feasibility
* Strong attention to detail and ability to produce polished, developer\-ready designs
* Strong written and spoken English
* Ability to work independently in a remote environment


**Strongly Preferred Experience**
* Experience designing marketplace platforms or multi\-sided products
* Experience with property technology, real estate platforms, maintenance platforms, field\-service software, booking platforms, fintech, CRM systems, or enterprise workflow software
* Experience designing products with multiple user types and role\-based permissions
* Experience designing payment, transaction, vendor, booking, service\-request, or dashboard workflows
* Experience designing AI\-powered product features or AI\-assisted workflows
* Experience improving an existing product rather than only designing from scratch
* Experience working in startups or fast\-moving product environments
* Experience with usability testing, product analytics, user research, or customer feedback loops
* Experience creating design systems from the ground up


 AI Expectations
   

  

 We are looking for a designer who uses AI as a productivity tool, not as a substitute for product judgment.
   

  

**You Should Be Comfortable Using AI To Help With**
* UX research organization
* User\-flow exploration
* Wireframe ideation
* Interface\-copy options
* Product requirement organization
* Edge\-case discovery
* Design\-system documentation
* Competitive research summaries
* Prototype concepts
* Usability\-test summaries
* Design iteration


 However, you must still review, validate, and improve all AI\-assisted work yourself. Final design decisions must be based on user needs, product logic, business goals, usability, accessibility, and technical feasibility.
   

  

 The Person We Are Looking For
   

  

 You are a true product thinker.
   

  

 You do not just make screens look good — you understand how people actually use software.
   

  

 You can take a complicated workflow and make it feel clear, simple, and logical.
   

  

 You are comfortable designing for different types of users who each need different information, permissions, dashboards, and actions.
   

  

 You think through edge cases, empty states, errors, mobile responsiveness, role\-based access, data\-heavy screens, and developer handoff.
   

  

 You are confident working with engineers and leadership, and you can explain why a design decision matters.
   

  

 You are also comfortable using AI to work faster, explore more options, and improve your process, while still owning the quality of the final product.
   

  

 What Success Looks Like
   

  

* The platform becomes easier to understand and easier to use
* Core workflows are redesigned with clearer user journeys
* Web and mobile experiences become more consistent and polished
* Developers receive clear, complete, buildable design specifications
* The design system becomes scalable and reusable
* Product screens feel modern, professional, and commercially ready
* Users can complete important tasks with less confusion and fewer unnecessary steps
* AI is used responsibly to improve speed, quality, and documentation
* Design work directly supports product launch and long\-term platform growth


**Compensation**
 The monthly compensation range for this role is:
   

  

 CAD $24,000–$36,000 annually
   

  

 Final compensation will depend on experience, product\-design depth, SaaS and marketplace experience, AI\-assisted workflow capability, communication skills, and ability to work independently.

title: User Experience Analyst
description:
**Role:** 
 UI/UX Analyst (D2C Product)
 



**Reports To:** 
 Lead D2C
 



**Location:** 
 Mumbai (Work from Office)
 



  





**Nature of Business \& What You'll Own** 




 As UI/UX Analyst, you'll
 **diagnose friction, design better user experiences, and validate improvements through data.** 




 You're not a pure designer. You're not a pure analyst. You're the
 **bridge** 
 – using session recordings, heatmaps, and funnel data to identify
 *why* 
 customers drop off, and designing solutions to test.
 



  





**Key Responsibilities** 



1. Session recording analysis \- watch session recordings 2–3x/week to spot friction and user behavior patterns
2. UX friction diagnosis – combine session data, heatmaps, and GA4 to build a prioritized list of improvements
3. A/B test variant design – sketch solutions in Figma based on your findings; collaborate with the product and design teams on testing strategy
4. Design system maintenance — collaborate with the design strategy team to document components and ensure consistency across the website
5. Insight reporting – weekly conversion updates to the team; monthly deep dives on major findings
6. Tool evaluation – research and recommend new UX testing tools (UserTesting, Maze, etc.) as you identify gaps in our workflow



 You'll collaborate closely with the product and engineering teams to drive user\-centric improvements across the platform.
 



  





**Technical Capabilities Required:** 




**Design Tools \& Prototyping:** 



* **Figma proficiency** 
 (non\-negotiable) – component\-based design, design systems, interactive prototypes
* Ability to create A/B test variants quickly and hand off clean specs to engineering
* Understanding of mobile\-first design



**Analytics \& Data Tools( good to have):** 



* **GA4** 
 –funnel visualization, event tracking, custom reports (not deep SQL, but comfortable navigating the tool)
* **Session recording tools** 
 – session recording, heatmaps, and user behavior identification
* Ability to interpret data and translate findings into design improvements
* Basic statistical thinking (correlation vs. causation, sample size matters)



**Platform \& E\-Commerce Context:** 



* Familiarity of
 **e\-commerce platforms** 
 – enough to know what's possible and what's a technical constraint
* Familiarity with
 **conversion funnel** 
 – browse → add\-to\-cart → checkout → payment → confirmation



**Tools You Can Learn \& Suggest:** 



* You're encouraged to research and recommend new tools that fit your workflow –
 **UserTesting, Maze, Hotjar, Pendo** 
 , etc.
* You should stay current on UX testing and session recording tools



  





**Functional Capabilities Required:** 




**Conversion Psychology:** 



* Understand micro\-interactions that drive decision\-making (button color, copy, social proof, urgency)
* Know how to reduce friction (form fields, payment options, trust signals)
* Apply JTBD (Jobs to Be Done) thinking – what job is the customer hiring this product for?



**UX Research \& Data Literacy:** 



* Can read a session recording and identify 3–5 UX issues
* Can spot patterns in heatmap data (click clusters, scroll depth, attention areas)
* Comfortable asking "why" – always validate assumptions with data before designing



**A/B Testing \& Iteration:** 



* Design test variants based on hypothesis, not guesswork
* Understand statistical rigor (sample size, test duration, confidence levels)
* Iterate based on results – learn from losses, compound wins



**Communication \& Collaboration:** 



* Sketch ideas quickly in Figma and get feedback early
* Present findings to product and design teams in a structured way
* Comfortable with ambiguity — you'll be expected to own problems, not just execute specs



  





**Required Skills \& Experience:** 



* **2–3 years** 
 of UX/UI design or product analytics experience (agency, SaaS, e\-commerce, or D2C preferred)
* **Figma expertise** 
 \- can create designs, components, and interactive prototypes; not a designer by training, but by fluency
* **Conversion psychology** 
 – understand how small UX changes impact user behavior
* **Data literacy** 
 – comfortable with GA4 funnels, segment analysis, and session recording tools
* **Mobile\-first thinking** 
 – design for phones first, then desktop
* **India D2C context** 
 – nice\-to\-have but not mandatory. Understanding of Indian customer behavior, payment methods, and logistics is valuable
* **Written communication** 
 — can document findings clearly and present to non\-designers



  





**To apply , please complete the following 2 questions:** 




  





**Task 1 Description:** 




 Audit The Whole Truth Foods' website (thewholetruthfoods.com), specifically the
 **product browse → add\-to\-cart → checkout flow** 
 . Identify 4\-5 friction points or UX issues that could impact conversion rate. For 2 of these issues, design a proposed improvement in Figma or any free design tool (Penpot, Excalidraw, Figma free tier). Include a written analysis explaining:
 


* What friction you identified (and why it matters)
* How you'd measure the impact of your proposed change
* Hypothesis for what conversion lift you'd expect



  





**Task 2 Description:** 




 Your GA4 shows that 42% of users land on the homepage, but only 18% click into a category page. Of those who do, only 8% complete a purchase. Heatmap data shows the category navigation menu has low click\-through \- users instead using the search bar. Session recordings reveal users are confused about the difference between similar products (e.g., Whey Protein vs. Plant Protein, or different protein bar flavors). The exit rate on category pages is 35%."
 



**Candidate's Task:** 



1. **Diagnose the issue** 
 – Write 150–200 words on why category navigation is underperforming and how it impacts the funnel (consider: information overload, product differentiation, filtering options, trust signals)
2. **Propose 3 design/UX changes** 
 — Could include: improved category page layout, better filtering, comparison tools, simplified navigation, product badge/labeling, etc.
3. **Design 1 variant** 
 – Redesigned category page or navigation menu in Figma/free tool
4. **Testing \& insights plan** 
 – How would you test? What secondary metrics matter (e.g., time on category page, filter usage, comparison tool clicks)?

 You will design the static ads that run our Meta account. Not brand posts, not moodboards, not one hero image a week. title: Business Designer
description:
TinkerLabs is a behavioural design firm in Mumbai. For over a decade, we've helped organisations understand people and design interventions that change what they do.
 



  





 We're good at the human side. We don't always ask early enough whether the business can carry it: what it costs, who pays, and whether it lasts.
 



  





 That's the gap this role fills, in our clients' work and in our own. The job has two halves.
 



  





**Outward** 
 , you'll be the business and feasibility voice inside deeply user\-focused work, on projects spanning sales transformation, customer insight, financial inclusion and public health.
 



  





**Inward** 
 , TinkerLabs will be your client too. We're in a growth phase with more doors open than we can walk through. You'll work alongside the founder to decide which ones matter. Then you'll build the systems, from how we sell to how we deliver, that let us walk through them without breaking.
 



  




**What you'll do** 

  





**On client work** 




**Be the viability voice.** 
 Sit inside behavioural research and design projects and hold the commercial question open: unit economics, cost to serve, market size, competitive dynamics, what the client's P\&L can actually absorb. Not as the final gate at the end. From the first week, alongside the researchers.
 



  





**Conduct real business research.** 
 Market and category analysis, competitor mapping, business model teardowns, secondary data, expert conversations. Our user research is strong. This is the other half of the picture, and we want it just as rigorous.
 



  





**Design the model, not just the solution.** 
 Value propositions, revenue models, pricing, go\-to\-market, service blueprints. Turn a good idea into something with a path to being real.
 



  





**Facilitate.** 
 Co\-creation sessions with clients, and workshops for corporate and academic audiences. You'll be in front of a room regularly.
 



  





**On TinkerLabs** 




**Look far, look near: help us choose where to grow.** 
 We have more avenues than capacity: new sectors, new clients, new offerings, new ways to package what we know. You'll work with the core team to size them, pressure\-test them and pick. Then you'll work out the how: what it takes, who does it, and in what order.
 



  





**Be systematic, like a mathematics professor.** 
 Treat the firm as a design problem. How does a lead become a proposal? How does a proposal become a priced, staffed project? How does that project run week to week and close well? Too much of our work lives in people's heads. You'll map how we actually work, find where it breaks, and redesign it.
 



  





**Build the pitch and the narrative.** 
 Approach notes, proposals, positioning. This includes the question every firm like ours is being asked right now: what does AI change about what we do, and where do we stand? We have a point of view forming. You'll help us sharpen it.
 



  





 The split between the two halves will shift. Some months will be mostly client work, others mostly internal.
 



  




 Who we need
 
  





 Our team has come from anthropology, psychology, design, engineering, architecture and business. Your background matters less than what it lets you do. That said, you should bring:
 



  





**3\+ years in the right kind of room.** 
 Strategy consulting, business design, product strategy, growth, venture building, corporate strategy or founder's office. An MBA is welcome, not required.
 



  





**Real commercial instinct.** 
 You can look at a business and quickly see how it makes money and where that breaks.
 



  





**Systems you've built that people actually used.** 
 Processes, pipelines, pricing models, project rhythms. Not decks about systems. Bonus if you did it inside a firm that was growing while you built it.
 



  





**The ability to turn a half\-formed question into a plan.** 
 A lot of the internal work will start as a hunch. You'll need to shape it, push back when it's the wrong question, and see it through.
 



  





**The ability to hold a room.** 
 From a CXO challenging your numbers to a client's frontline team wondering why you're there.
   




 What is in it for you (beside the core role)
 
  






 We don't stop at the deck. We find the behaviour, design the intervention, put it in the field, and stay until it works. You'll see the whole arc, from the first insight to whether it actually worked.
 




  





 We're small and growing fast. Whoever joins now shapes what we become.
 



  





 Here's what that means concretely.
 



**You'll design the firm, not just the projects.** 
 You'll decide which sectors we go after, how we sell, how we price and how we deliver, working directly with the core team.
 



  





**You'll get range you won't find anywhere else.** 
 We've worked with Microsoft, HUL, Flipkart, Swiggy, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Vodafone, The Oberoi Group, GAP and Raymond. We've also worked with PATH, UNFPA, GIZ, Population Council, Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Gates Foundation. Banking, retail, public health, technology, hospitality, gender, education. A sales transformation one month, financial inclusion for low\-income women the next.
 



  





**You'll have a seat at the centre of the work.** 
 You won't be handed insights to monetise. You'll be in the research, in the design, and in the pitch.
 



  





**You'll join a team that makes you better.** 
 Small, sharp, supportive, and serious about craft.
 



  




 How to apply
 
  





 Besides sharing your CV, please respond to two short prompts. We're interested in how you think, not how polished it looks.
 


1. Pick a product or service you think is genuinely well designed but commercially broken. What's wrong with the model, and what would you change?
2. AI is changing what clients will pay consultants for. Using real evidence, tell us what's losing value, what's gaining value, and where a firm like ours should stand.



  





 Answer in any format that does the thinking justice.
 



  





 Send your responses, updated CV and portfolio to curious@tinkerlabs.in with the subject line
 **Business Designer\_(Your name)** 
 .
 



  





*A human reads every application. You'll hear back from us either way.*

* Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Corporate Training, or a related field.

description:

* 🎬 Edit

**Come create what’s next with us.**

  Freshers to experienced —

***About the Role***




*Submarine Pens Ltd* 
**.** 
 is looking for a Graphic Designer to shape how our brands look, feel, and tell their story, across packaging and communication design. We're less focused on years of experience and more on whether your work has a distinct point of view: strong storytelling instincts, a good eye for aesthetics, and the range to move between different brand personalities without losing craft.
 



 You'll be working across a portfolio of brands with different visual identities, so versatility matters as much as individual style.
 



  





***Key Responsibilities***



* Design packaging for a range of product lines \- from concept through print\-ready files, with an understanding of materials, finishes, and production constraints.
* Design communication assets: social media creatives, brand decks, website visuals, retail collateral, and campaign material
* Translate brand positioning and tone into visual language — you'll be handed a brand's story and personality, and need to design something that actually feels like it
* Maintain visual consistency and brand guideline compliance across multiple sub\-brands with distinct identities
* Collaborate with the marketing team on creative direction for launches and campaigns
* Occasionally support building out visual identity systems for new product lines or brand extensions



  





***Requirements***



* A strong portfolio that demonstrates storytelling and aesthetic sensibility (
 *this matters more to us than a specific degree or number of years worked)*
* Proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite (CorelDraw, Illustrator, Photoshop, at minimum)
* Understanding of print production fundamentals for packaging (dielines, CMYK, finishes, material considerations)
* Ability to work across multiple visual identities without diluting brand distinctiveness
* Good instincts for composition, typography, and colour — the kind of eye that's hard to teach.

* Prior experience designing for premium or luxury brands
* Familiarity with retail packaging specifically
* Basic motion graphics or video editing skills.
* Experience working across a multi\-brand portfolio



  





***What We Offer***



* Exposure to both packaging and communication design, rather than being siloed into one
* Room to bring your own aesthetic point of view to the work



  





***How to Apply***




 Please submit your portfolio (link or PDF) along with your resume. We'll be looking closely at the portfolio. Show
 
 us relevant work, that you're proudest of.
